items.title: Joe Bushkin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: my group with Buck Clayton, Milt Hinton and Jo Jones

ctx.x: You mean for the audience, if their bill was 20 bucks, there was a 20 percent tax on that as the war tax? © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -8-

Right. But there was no tax for instrumental groups. So if a guy showed up with a party of six or eight and racked up a tab for a C note or whatever, that twenty dollars took care of the waiter’s tip and the cab ride. And so we did a lot of business, based on the fact that during the 26 week scene, we had Red Norvo’s trio and my group. I was there for the whole 26 weeks and whatever you want to call it, I was considered the draw in the place. And then we had Teddy Wilson and a group, and actually that was a…

items.title: 67246_Buck Clayton oral history interview
items.q: Then, I was also playing in the Embers Club with Joe Bushkin off and on.

ctx.x: In between I would play with different guys, different bands. I played with Jimmy Rushing's band for a while. He had a good band, yes. He had myself, Emmett Berry, Dickie Wells, Buddy Tate. Then he had, I don't remember who in the heck we had on the, on the rhythm now, but he had a good band, very good. And we were all writing for the band. Dickie was writing, I was writing. And I played there for, we played up there

for quite a while.
Then, I was also playing in the Embers Club with Joe Bushkin off and on.
Well now, was that the sort of the beginning of that muted trumpet thing with rhythm that Jonah Jones got into to?
